01The Loss

A gap is not just a gap. The moment a tooth comes out, the bone that held it has nothing left to do — and bone that has nothing to do disappears.

That is why waiting is the expensive option. The longer the site is empty, the more likely it is that the jaw has to be rebuilt before an implant can go in at all.

02The Answer

Why are dental implants the best solution?

Dental implants are often the best solution for tooth loss because they replace the root as well as the tooth — which is what keeps the jawbone underneath working.

  1. 01 Look natural The crown is matched to the colour, shape and size of the teeth around it. Nobody can tell which one it is.
  2. 02 Don't hurt The area is fully numbed, and sedation is available for every implant procedure we place.
  3. 03 Easy to take care of Brush it and floss it like a real tooth. No adhesives, no soaking, nothing to take out.
  4. 04 Keep your mouth healthy The implant stimulates the bone the way a root does, so the jaw doesn't shrink away under the gap.
  5. 05 Can last a lifetime Implants have been documented surviving nearly 40 years. Cared for properly, this is a once-only repair.
  6. 06 Leave your other teeth alone A bridge means filing down the healthy teeth on both sides of the gap. An implant leaves them alone.

03The Options

One tooth, several teeth, or a full arch

Implant dentistry is one of the most technically demanding procedures in all of dentistry. What you need depends on what is left to work with — that is what the consultation is for.

01

Single implant crown

The most natural way to replace one missing tooth. A custom crown on your own implant, matched to the teeth beside it.

02

Implant bridge

Two implants anchor a bridge across several missing teeth in a row — without filing down the healthy teeth either side.

03

All-on-X full arch

Four to six strategically placed implants support a full arch of fixed, non-removable teeth.

04

Failing implant rescue

Pain, looseness, infection, or an implant that just doesn't look right — placed somewhere else. We can help.

04The Candidacy

Do I need dental implants?

Are you missing one or more of your teeth? Regular brushing, flossing, and preventive checkups allow some people to maintain their natural smiles for a lifetime. However, sometimes our teeth just can't stand up to the everyday wear and tear we put on them.

Tooth loss can be caused by oral trauma due to an accident, illness, stress, age, decay, and more. Sometimes it's just bad luck that causes someone to suffer the loss of a tooth. If you want to know more, Dr. Will Sung and his team are there to help at Grand Mission Dentistry, Richmond, TX.

  • You're missing one or more teeth, or one is about to come out
  • You want something permanent rather than something that comes out at night
  • You'd rather not file down the healthy teeth on either side of the gap
  • You've been told elsewhere that you're not a candidate — get a free second opinion

Preliminary procedures

Sometimes the site has to be prepared first

After your consultation, Dr. Sung may recommend one of these before the implant goes in. It isn't a setback — it's what makes the implant last.

01

Bone graft

Rebuilds jawbone that has shrunk away since the tooth was lost, so the implant has something solid to anchor into.

02

Socket preservation

Done at the time of extraction. Fills and protects the socket so the bone holds its shape while it heals.

03

Gum tissue regeneration

Restores the gum around the site, which is what gives the finished crown a natural margin instead of a visible line.

04

Ridge augmentation

Widens or heightens a jaw ridge that has flattened, usually after a tooth has been missing for a long time.

A single-tooth dental implant involves a titanium post surgically placed in your jaw to act as an artificial tooth root. Once healed, the implant is topped with a custom-made dental crown, restoring the appearance and function of your natural tooth.

Dr. Sung will evaluate your dental health and recommend the best solution for replacing your missing tooth. Single-tooth dental implants are ideal for patients seeking a permanent, natural-looking, and functional replacement for a lost tooth.

Bring the plan you were given and take the free second opinion. There is no cost and no pressure — sometimes bone grafting or ridge augmentation makes an implant possible after all, and sometimes a different restoration is genuinely the better answer.
